The line graph gives information about the employment of American workers in various sectors
from 1930 to 2010.
Overall, throughout the given period, the industrial, technical, and sales & office sectors emerged
as major employers. In contrast, there was a sharp downward trend in the number of people
working in the agricultural sector, becoming the least Chosen one by the end of the timeframe.
Regarding industries that gained in popularity, in 1930, virtually no Americans were engaged in
industrial and technical jobs, and only 10% pursued sales and office occupations. Thereafter,
having remained consistent until 1960, industrial sector began attracting more
workers, with its percentages rising gradually\to a peak of roughly 35% in both 2000 and 2010.
Similar upward trends were also witnessed in technical and sales and office positions, as their
participation rates underwent steady increases overall, to around 30% and 20% respectively in
the final year, making them the second and third most common occupations.
On the other hand, despite being the dominant industry in 1930, with approximately 75% of the
labor force employed in farming, fishing and foresting, this sector saw a dramatic decline over
the years, reaching a low of only 5% in 2010. Finally, the workers in

other services rose
stable level of around 10% for the rest of the period.
